Start Debug (STRDBG) - Help :P. The Start Debug (STRDBG) command puts a job into debug mode and, optionally, adds as many as 20 programs and 20 service programs and 20 class files to debug mode. It also specifies certain attributes of the debugging session. For example, it can specify whether database files in production libraries can be updated while in debug mode. :P. The graphical system debugger will be launched instead of the traditional system debugger if the STRDBG command is issued by a user registered for graphical debugging. :P. Debug can operate in three environments at the same time. They are OPM (Original Program Model), ILE (Integrated Language Environment), and JAVA. Some parameters for this command are applicable for all three environments. Some parameters for this command are applicable only for OPM, ILE, or JAVA. There will be a statement in each parameter description stating the environment in which the parameter is applicable. :P. The Change Debug (CHGDBG) command can be used later in the job to change the attributes of the debug mode. Also, OPM programs can be added to or removed from the debugging session if they are specified in the Add Program (ADDPGM) or Remove Program (RMVPGM) commands. OPM programs added with the ADDPGM command will be in the OPM debug environment. :P. When one job is servicing another job, and STRDBG is entered, all debug commands are valid for the job being serviced. If that job is held on a job queue, no further debug commands may be entered until that job is allowed to run. When the job starts, an initial breakpoint screen is displayed. From this screen, additional debug commands may be entered. To service another job, see the STRSRVJOB (Start Service Job) command. More information about debugging one job from another job is in the CL Programming book, SC41-5721. :P. :HP2.Restrictions::EHP2. :UL. :LI.You cannot use this command in debug mode. Before a program can be debugged, its name must be specified on this parameter, in the Add Program (ADDPGM) command, or the Display Module Source (DSPMODSRC) command. :P. This parameter is applicable in both OPM and ILE environments. .* :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.*NONE:EPK. :PD.No program names are specified at the start of the debugging session. The Add Program (ADDPGM) command or the Display Module Source (DSPMODSRC) command can be used to add programs later.
:PT.:PV.program-name:EPV. :PD.Specify the names of up to 20 programs to debug. You cannot debug two programs that have the same name at the same time in the OPM debug environment. In the ILE debug environment, two programs with the same name can be debugged if they are in different libraries.
:PT.:PV.program-type:EPV. :PD.Specify what type of program you want to debug.
:EPARML. :P. The possible library values are: .* :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.*LIBL:EPK. :PD.All libraries in the library list for the current thread are searched until the first match is found.
:PT.:PV.*CURLIB:EPV. :PD.The current library for the job is used to locate the program. If no library is specified as the current library for the job, QGPL is used.
:PT.:PV.library-name:EPV. :PD.Specify the library where the program is located.
:EPARML. :P. The possible program type values are: .* :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.*AUTO:EPK. :PD.The type of the program is automatically determined. The STRDBG command searches the first program or service program that matches the specified name and starts the debugger for it. Program objects are found before service program objects.

:PT.:PV.*SRVPGM:EPV. :PD.The specified program name is considered to be a service program object.
:EPARML. .* :EHELP. .* .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- .* Hilfetext für Schlüsselwort PGM .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- :HELP name='STRDBG/DFTPGM '. Default program (DFTPGM) - Help :XH3.Default program (DFTPGM) :P. Specifies the name of the OPM program to use as the default program during debug mode. The program specified here is used as the default program for any of the other debug commands for which the user specified a value of *DFTPGM for the :HP2.Program (PGM):EHP2. parameter. That is, if a default program was previously specified, this parameter can change it. :P. This parameter is applicable only in the OPM environment. .* :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.*PGM:EPK. :PD.The program named on the PGM parameter of this command is to be the default program for the job's debugging session. If there is more than one program name specified on the PGM parameter, the first OPM program named in the list that is added to the OPM debug environment is the default program. If *NONE is specified on the PGM parameter, or is the default, *NONE is also assumed when this value (*PGM) is specified.
:PT.:PV.*NONE:EPV. :PD.No program is specified as the default program; if a program was specified as a default program, it is no longer the default program. If the job has no default program, *DFTPGM cannot be specified on the PGM parameter of any other debug commands.
:PT.:PV.program-name:EPV. :PD.Specify the name of the program to use as the default program during debug mode. The same name (in qualified form) must also be specified for the PGM parameter of this command. You cannot specify a bound program on this parameter. :SL. :LI.:HP2.Note::EHP2. If OPMSRC(*YES) is specified, the OPM program may be added to either the OPM debug environment or the ILE debug environment. If added to the ILE debug environment, then it cannot be a default program for the OPM debug environment. :ESL.
:EPARML. .* :EHELP. .* .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- .* Hilfetext für Schlüsselwort MAXTRC .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- :HELP name='STRDBG/MAXTRC '. Maximum trace statements (MAXTRC) - Help :XH3.Maximum trace statements (MAXTRC) :P. Specifies the maximum number of trace statements that the system puts into the job's trace file before either stopping tracing or wrapping around (overlaying) on the trace file. When the trace file contains the maximum specified, the system performs the actions specified by the value supplied for the :HP2.Trace full (TRCFULL):EHP2. parameter. :SL. :LI.:HP2.Note::EHP2. Instruction stepping can be performed on a program being debugged in an interactive environment by setting the maximum number of trace statements to :HP2.1:EHP2. and the value for the TRCFULL parameter to *STOPTRC. :ESL. :P. This parameter is applicable only in the OPM environment. .* :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.200:EPK. :PD.Two hundred trace statements can be put into the file before tracing is stopped or wrapping occurs.
:PT.:PV.maximum-trace-statements:EPV. :PD.Specify the maximum number of trace statements that can be in the trace file.
:EPARML. .* :EHELP. .* .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- .* Hilfetext für Schlüsselwort TRCFULL .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- :HELP name='STRDBG/TRCFULL '. Trace full (TRCFULL) - Help :XH3.Trace full (TRCFULL) :P. Specifies what happens when the job's trace file is full (that is, it contains the maximum number of trace statements specified by the value supplied for the :HP2.Maximum trace statements (MAXTRC):EHP2. parameter. :P. This parameter is applicable only in the OPM environment. .* :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.*STOPTRC:EPK. :PD.In a batch environment, tracing stops but the program continues processing. In an interactive environment, control is given to the user when a breakpoint occurs. If the user continues processing, a breakpoint occurs before processing each subsequent statement within the range of statements being traced, and the trace file is extended to contain the new entry.
:PT.:PV.*WRAP:EPV. :PD.The trace file is overlaid with new trace statements as they occur, wrapping from the beginning of the file. The program will complete processing with no message to indicate that wrapping has occurred. The trace file never has more than the maximum specified statements, and they are the most recently recorded statements.
:EPARML. .* :EHELP. .* .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- .* Hilfetext für Schlüsselwort UPDPROD .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- :HELP name='STRDBG/UPDPROD '. Update production files (UPDPROD) - Help :XH3.Update production files (UPDPROD) :P. Specifies whether or not database files in a production library can be opened for updating records, or for adding new records, while the job is in debug mode. If not, the files must be copied into a test library before trying to run a program that uses the files. :P. This parameter is applicable in both OPM and ILE environments. .* :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.*NO:EPK. :PD.Database files in production libraries cannot be updated while the job is in debug mode. Database files can be opened for reading only. This protects database files from unwanted updates while a program is being debugged. The exception to this is starting debug mode after a production library is already opened. If this value is specified, some commands, which may include function keys, menu options, or pulldowns, may not work properly.
:PT.:PV.*YES:EPV. :PD.Database files in production libraries can be updated while the job is in debug mode.
:EPARML. .* :EHELP. .* .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- .* Hilfetext für Schlüsselwort OPMSRC .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- :HELP name='STRDBG/OPMSRC '. OPM source level debug (OPMSRC) - Help :XH3.OPM source level debug (OPMSRC) :P. Specifies that OPM programs are debugged using the system source debug support (same as ILE source debug). :P. This parameter is valid for OPM CL, OPM RPG and OPM COBOL programs that were created with OPTION(*SRCDBG) with CRTCLPGM, CRTRPGPGM and CRTCBLPGM commands. Additionally, this parameter is valid for OPM CL, OPM RPG and OPM COBOL programs that were created with OPTION(*LSTDBG) with the CRTCLPGM, CRTRPGPGM, CRTCBLPGM, CRTSQLRPG, CRTSQLCBL, and CRTRPTRPG commands. If the OPM program is not CL, RPG or COBOL and was not compiled with a valid debug option, then this parameter is ignored. :P. This parameter is applicable in both OPM and ILE environment. :P. ILE functions will now operate on OPM programs. For example, source level debug. .* :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.*NO:EPK. :PD.OPM debug functions are used for OPM programs.
:PT.:PV.*YES:EPV. :PD.ILE debug functions are used for OPM programs.
:EPARML. .* :EHELP. .* .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- .* Hilfetext für Schlüsselwort SRVPGM .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- :HELP name='STRDBG/SRVPGM '. Service program (SRVPGM) - Help :XH3.Service program (SRVPGM) :P. Specifies the qualified names of up to 20 service programs to debug in the job. Before a service program can be debugged, its name must be specified on this parameter or the Display Module Source (DSPMODSRC) command. :P. This parameter is applicable only in the ILE environment. .* :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.*NONE:EPK. :PD.No service program names are specified at the start of the debugging session. The Display Module Source (DSPMODSRC) command can be used to add service programs later.
:PT.:PV.service-program-name:EPV. :PD.Specify the names of up to 20 service programs to debug.
:EPARML. :P. The possible library values are: .* :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.*LIBL:EPK. :PD.All libraries in the library list for the current thread are searched until the first match is found.
:PT.:PV.*CURLIB:EPV. :PD.The current library for the job is used to locate the service program. If no library is specified as the current library for the job, QGPL is used.
:PT.:PV.library-name:EPV. :PD.Specify the library where the service program is located.
:EPARML. .* :EHELP. .* .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- .* Hilfetext für Schlüsselwort CLASS .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- :HELP name='STRDBG/CLASS '. Class file (CLASS) - Help :XH3.Class file (CLASS) :P. Specifies the names of up to 20 class files to debug in the job. Before a class file can be debugged, its name must be specified on this parameter or the Display Module Source (DSPMODSRC) command. :P. This parameter is applicable only in the ILE environment. .* :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.*NONE:EPK. :PD.No class files are specified at the start of the debugging session. The Display Module Source (DSPMODSRC) command can be used to add class files later.
:PT.:PV.class-file-name:EPV. :PD.Specify the names of up to 20 class files to debug.
:EPARML. .* :EHELP. .* .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- .* Hilfetext für Schlüsselwort JOB .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- :HELP name='STRDBG/JOB '. Job name (JOB) - Help :XH3.Job name (CLASS) :P. Specifies the job to be serviced. If no job number is given, all of the jobs currently in the system are searched for the simple job name. If duplicates of the specified name are found, a subfile is shown and the desired job must be selected. The job name entered cannot be the name of the job issuing the command. :P. This parameter is applicable in both OPM and ILE environment. :P. :HP2.Qualifier 1: Job name:EHP2. .* :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.*:EPK. :PD.The debugger is started for the current job. No service job is started.
:PT.:PV.*ALL:EPV. :PD.Specifies that all jobs of the user who is specified for the:HP2.User:EHP2. qualifier are applicable for selection. If duplicate jobs are found for the user, a subfile is shown and the desired job must be selected. The number of applicable jobs might also be limited by specifying a value for the :HP2.Number:EHP2. qualifier.
:PT.:PV.name:EPV. :PD.Specify the name of the job. :EPARML. :P. :HP2.Qualifier 2: User:EHP2. .* :PARML. :PT.:PV.*ALL:EPV. :PD.Specifies that all jobs of the user are applicable for selection. The number of applicable jobs might also be limited by specifying a value for the :HP2.Number:EHP2. qualifier.
:PT.:PV.name:EPV. :PD.Specify the user name that identifies the user profile under which the job was run. :EPARML. :P. :HP2.Qualifier 3: Number:EHP2. .* :PARML. :PT.:PV.*ALL:EPV. :PD.Specifies that all jobs are applicable for selection. The number of jobs can be limited by specifying values for the:HP2.User:EHP2. qualifier and :HP2.Name:EHP2. qualifier.
:PT.:PV.000000-999999:EPV. :PD.Specify the system-assigned job number of the job to be serviced. :EPARML. .* :EHELP. .* .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- .* Hilfetext für Schlüsselwort WIDESCN .*-------------------------------------------------------------------- :HELP name='STRDBG/WIDESCN '. Allow wide screen (WIDESCN) - Help :XH3.Allow wide screen (WIDESCN) :P. Specifies the screen mode for the debugger. Normally the debugger starts in 24 mode. This parameter allows to start the debugger in 27 2 mode. :P. :PARML. :PT.:PK DEF.*PRV:EPK. :PD.Start the debugger using the previous screen mode. Actually the debugger uses the value of the :HP2.ILE_DEBUGGER_1:EHP2. environment variable to determine the screen mode. Since this environment variable is usually deleted on signoff, the debugger might start in 24 mode after signon although it was last started in 27 2 mode.
:PT.:PV.*NO:EPV. :PD.Switches to 24 mode.
:PT.:PV.*YES:EPV. :PD.Enables wide screen mode and switches to 27 2 mode.
